page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core. The processor cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities and high memory bandwidth. The c8gn.12xlarge achieves top-tier performance in large-block memory bandwidth, registering 402.56 GB/sec for read operations and 198.42 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core performance is also highly rated, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching 23,747.0 and software compilation with Clang scoring in the top tier at 70,375.0. Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput of 101.03 GB/sec also place in the top tier. Conversely, single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the average category. Large language model text generation performance varies, showing weak throughput for small models at 68.61 tokens/sec but strong throughput for medium 7B models at 36.59 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8gn.12xlarge leverages the ARMv9 architecture to deliver high multi-threaded compute density and memory throughput without the overhead of hyperthreading. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes, which represents a structural tradeoff for disk-heavy operations. This instance is suited for network-intensive and compute-bound workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, database operations, and medium-scale language model inference.
description: The Amazon Web Services c8gn.12xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized server powered by 48 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 96.0 GB of memory and a 150 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks show top-tier performance in large-block memory bandwidth, software compilation, and static web serving throughput, alongside strong multi-core processing. However, single-core performance and small-model text generation remain average to weak. This resource profile offers high compute density and memory throughput, making it suitable for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database operations, and high-bandwidth web serving, while requiring network-attached storage for disk-heavy tasks.
